messages:
maria: Hey team — compliance asked for a single artefact set showing KMS usage + rotation + IAM changes across AWS/GCP/Azure for the SOC2 audit. Does anyone have a short checklist or queries we can run?

kevin: I can sketch a checklist. High level: (1) Key inventory (ARN/IDs, creation dates, rotation enabled flag), (2) Key usage events (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext/ReEncrypt), (3) Key policy / IAM changes (SetIamPolicy, PutKeyPolicy, roleAssignment writes), (4) Rotation events or proof of automated rotation, (5) Exported audit log snapshots + checksums, (6) Mapping between service principals and key usage.

samir: +1. For AWS specifically you can query CloudTrail/S3 with Athena. Example Athena SQL to pull KMS events: 
```
SELECT eventtime, eventname, useridentity.principalid, awsregion, requestparameters, responseelements 
FROM cloudtrail_logs 
WHERE eventsource = 'kms.amazonaws.com' 
  AND eventname IN ('Encrypt','Decrypt','GenerateDataKey','GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext','ReEncrypt') 
  AND eventtime BETWEEN timestamp '2026-02-01 00:00:00' AND timestamp '2026-02-28 23:59:59';
```
This gives us key usage without leaking any plaintext. Also look for EnableKeyRotation and DisableKeyRotation.

elaine: For GCP, use Cloud Logging (Audit Logs). Example filter in Logs Explorer: 
```resource.type="cloudkms_key_ring" protoPayload.methodName:("Encrypt" OR "Decrypt" OR "GenerateEncryptedKey") 
resource.labels.location="us-central1" timestamp>="2026-02-01T00:00:00Z"
```
Note method names include google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Encrypt etc. Export those logs to a secured GCS bucket (with bucket-level ACLs + CMEK) and capture an object digest (sha256).

kevin: Azure Key Vault: enable DiagnosticsSettings on vaults and send logs to Log Analytics / Storage. Query example in Log Analytics (KQL): 
```KeyVaultAuditEvents
| where TimeGenerated between(datetime(2026-02-01) .. datetime(2026-02-28))
| where OperationName has_any ("encrypt","decrypt","wrapKey","unwrapKey","backup")
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, CallerIpAddress, Identity, ResultType
```
Also capture 'RoleAssignments' operations under Microsoft.Authorization to show RBAC changes.

maria: Can we also capture proofs for rotation? AWS CMKs have a rotationEnabled flag but that only shows enabled/disabled. How do we show rotation actually happened?

samir: For envelope encryption, most rotation is on data keys (GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext) and you won't see plaintext. To show rotation: (a) export key metadata (key version IDs / key material creation dates for multi-version keys), (b) for AWS, schedule/EnableKeyRotation events and CloudTrail events when customers call ReEncrypt or GenerateDataKey that reference a new KeyId. If you use key aliases with timestamped versions, map usage to keyVersion ARNs.

elaine: In GCP, check CryptoKeyVersion states. Each CryptoKey has versions and you can list versions and creation times via gcloud: 
```gcloud kms keys versions list KEY --location=... --keyring=... --format=json```
Export that JSON as evidence.

kevin: Important: include proof of access boundary changes — who can call the KMS APIs. For AWS, query CloudTrail for CreatePolicy/AttachRolePolicy/PutRolePolicy/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy and include the policy blobs as artifacts. For GCP, include IAM policy diffs (AuditLog methodName SetIamPolicy) and for Azure include roleAssignment write events.

maria: Any gotchas for envelope encryption where logs are sparse? We use GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext a lot. Auditor might ask how to prove plaintext keys were never exposed.

samir: Right — logs never contain plaintext. Instead provide: the KMS API calls (GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext, Decrypt with KeyId), key policy + IAM (who can call Decrypt), and server-side code pointers (link to repo path) showing we call the KMS SDK correctly. Also provide unit test/eval that asserts we never call GenerateDataKey (with plaintext) in production flows.

elaine: Also include retention and tamper-evidence: store exported log bundles in a dedicated bucket/container with immutability settings (GCS retention policy / S3 Object Lock with governance/compliance mode). For each bundle, produce a manifest.json with sha256 checksums and PGP-sign the manifest (security-audit-bot can attest).

security-audit-bot: Attached evidence bundle created: s3://redwood-compliance/kms-audit/2026-02-bundle.tar.gz (sha256: b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184). Signature: SIGNATURE_PLACEHOLDER.

kevin: Nice. Also include cross-checks: sample decrypt/unwrap failures due to RBAC to show least privilege in action (capture the error event and the policy then).

maria: Action items: (1) Samir to export CloudTrail/KMS events for Feb 2026 + Athena query + checksum, (2) Elaine to export GCP CryptoKeyVersion list + logs to GCS and provide signed manifest, (3) Kevin to collect IAM policy diffs and Azure diagnostics queries. I'll attach all artifacts to the SOC2 ticket when we have them.

samir: Copy — will push Athena output to s3://redwood-compliance/kms-audit/aws/2026-02/ and upload manifest.

elaine: Uploading GCP exports now, will ping when signed manifest is ready.

kevin: I'll pull Azure blobs and roleAssignment logs and post checklist of queries.

maria: Thanks all — auditors gave a 48h window, let's aim to have uploads + manifests within 24h. :heart:

security-audit-bot: Reminder: please attach the manifest and checksums to JIRA ticket SEC-2026-14 before closing this thread.
